intent.raw_query: Istanbul cultural exploration, $1800 solo, historical sites and cuisine, May 2026

experiences.name: Hagia Sophia & Blue Mosque Exploration
experiences.description: Spend a morning exploring the iconic Hagia Sophia, a UNESCO World Heritage Site with nearly 1,500 years of history, then walk to the stunning Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Mosque) just across the square. Marvel at the Byzantine mosaics, massive domes, and intricate Iznik tile work. Entry to the Blue Mosque is free, while Hagia Sophia charges a modest fee.

experiences.name: Grand Bazaar & Spice Bazaar Immersion
experiences.description: Wander through the Grand Bazaar, one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets with over 4,000 shops, then head to the nearby Egyptian Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı) to sample Turkish delight, dried fruits, spices, and local teas. Haggle with vendors, sip complimentary çay (tea), and soak in centuries of trading culture.

experiences.name: Topkapi Palace & Harem Tour
experiences.description: Explore the sprawling Topkapi Palace, the administrative heart of the Ottoman Empire for nearly 400 years. Visit the Imperial Harem, treasury housing the Topkapi Dagger and Spoonmaker's Diamond, and enjoy panoramic views of the Bosphorus. A guided audio tour brings the rich Ottoman history vividly to life.

experiences.name: Traditional Turkish Food Tour in Karaköy & Beyoğlu
experiences.description: Join a guided street food walk through the vibrant neighborhoods of Karaköy and Beyoğlu. Taste simit (sesame bread rings), balık ekmek (fish sandwiches) by the Galata Bridge, börek (savory pastries), kokoreç, and finish with a classic Turkish breakfast spread at a local meyhane. Discover how food reflects Istanbul's multicultural heritage.

experiences.name: Bosphorus Cruise & Dolmabahçe Palace Visit
experiences.description: Take a scenic public ferry cruise along the Bosphorus Strait, witnessing the meeting point of Europe and Asia flanked by Ottoman palaces, yalıs (wooden mansions), and ancient fortresses. Disembark to tour the opulent Dolmabahçe Palace, the last residence of Ottoman sultans, featuring a 4.5-ton Bohemian crystal chandelier and lavish European-style interiors.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Istanbul
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Use arrival time to transfer from airport to Fatih Boutique Stay in Sultanahmet. Take the Marmaray train or metro for a budget-friendly transfer (~25-40 TL). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a gentle introductory walk around Sultanahmet Square. Admire the exterior of the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Mosque) and the Hippodrome of Constantinople. Stroll through the At Meydanı (Hippodrome) to see the Obelisk of Theodosius, the Serpent Column, and the German Fountain — all free to view.
day_by_day.evening: Wander down to the Arasta Bazaar near the Blue Mosque for a relaxed first evening browse. Watch the sunset over the Bosphorus from the nearby Sultanahmet Park benches. Enjoy the atmosphere as the mosques light up at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a quick simit (sesame bread ring) and çay (tea) from a street cart near the hotel for under 20 TL.
meals.lunch: Skip or grab a quick bite at the airport. Alternatively, try a local pide (Turkish flatbread) at a neighborhood fırın (bakery) near Sultanahmet for ~60-80 TL.
meals.dinner: Tarihi Sultanahmet Köftecisi — a legendary, no-frills köfte (meatball) restaurant steps from the hotel. A full meal with köfte, bread, and ayran costs ~120-150 TL. Budget classic.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Focus on settling in and soaking up the atmosphere. Exchange a small amount of currency at a reputable exchange office (döviz bürosu) near Sultanahmet rather than at the airport for better rates.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Hagia Sophia (Ayasofya) when it opens — arrive early to beat crowds. As a functioning mosque, entry is free. Marvel at the massive Byzantine dome, ancient mosaics, and layered history of this 1,500-year-old structure. Allow 1.5–2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Topkapi Palace complex. Purchase a Museum Pass Istanbul if planning multiple museum visits — it pays off quickly. Explore the Imperial Treasury, the Harem (separate ticket), and the palace courtyards with stunning Bosphorus views. Allow 3–4 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the Gülhane Park adjacent to Topkapi — free entry, beautiful gardens. Head to Eminönü waterfront to watch ferries and fishermen on the Galata Bridge.

meals.breakfast: Turkish breakfast (kahvaltı) at the hotel or a nearby kahvaltı salonu. Look for a set breakfast with olives, cheese, tomatoes, eggs, and tea for ~80-120 TL.
meals.lunch: Balık ekmek (fish sandwich) from the famous boats moored at Eminönü waterfront — ~60-80 TL. Eat standing by the water like a local.
meals.dinner: Lezzet-i Şark or a similar lokanta (traditional Turkish canteen) near Sultanahmet. Order ready-made dishes like lentil soup, rice, and a vegetable stew for ~100-130 TL total.

day_by_day.notes: Museum Pass Istanbul covers Topkapi Palace, Hagia Sophia Museum galleries, Istanbul Archaeological Museums, and more. If you plan to visit 3+ paid museums, it's excellent value. Check current pricing before purchase.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Istanbul Archaeological Museums — three museums in one complex next to Topkapi Palace. See the Alexander Sarcophagus, ancient Greek and Roman artifacts, and the Museum of the Ancient Orient. Covered by Museum Pass.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı) — an underground Byzantine cistern with atmospheric lighting and Medusa column bases. Admission fee applies (~200 TL, check current rates). Then walk to the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı) for a sensory overload of color, crafts, and commerce. Browse freely — no obligation to buy.
day_by_day.evening: Get lost in the backstreets of Beyazıt and Laleli neighborhoods near the Grand Bazaar. These areas have authentic local shops and tea houses away from tourist prices.

meals.breakfast: Börek from a local pastane (pastry shop) — flaky pastry filled with cheese or spinach, ~30-50 TL. Pair with a glass of çay.
meals.lunch: Soup kitchen style at a local çorba evi (soup house) near the Grand Bazaar. A hearty lentil soup with bread is ~40-60 TL.
meals.dinner: Develi or a similar kebab restaurant in Samatya/Fatih area. Try Adana or Urfa kebab with lavash bread and salad for ~150-180 TL.

day_by_day.notes: The Grand Bazaar is closed on Sundays, so Monday is perfect. Bargaining is expected in the bazaar but be respectful. Shopkeepers will often offer tea — accepting is fine and not obligating.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Camii) interior — free entry for non-worshippers outside prayer times. Admire the 20,000+ Iznik tiles and six minarets. Dress modestly (cover shoulders and knees; scarves available at entrance). Then visit the nearby Mosaic Museum (Büyük Saray Mozaikleri Müzesi) — covered by Museum Pass.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a tram (T1 line) to Beyoğlu. Walk up İstiklal Caddesi (Independence Avenue) — Istanbul's famous pedestrian boulevard with 19th-century architecture, street musicians, and local shops. Ride the historic Tünel funicular, one of the world's oldest underground railways (~15 TL).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Galata neighborhood. Climb the Galata Tower for panoramic city views (admission ~250 TL) or view it for free from the surrounding streets. Wander the bohemian streets around Galata with street art and independent cafés.

meals.breakfast: Van Kahvaltı Evi or similar Kurdish breakfast spot near Beyoğlu — a lavish spread of cheeses, honey, clotted cream, eggs, and herbs for ~150-200 TL. Worth the splurge for a full, authentic experience.
meals.lunch: Döner wrap from a local dürümcü on İstiklal or side streets — ~80-100 TL for a filling wrap.
meals.dinner: Karaköy Lokantası or a meyhane (Turkish tavern) in Karaköy with meze starters and a main. Budget ~200-250 TL with non-alcoholic drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Tram T1 connects Sultanahmet to Beyoğlu via Kabataş-Tünel. A single journey costs ~25-30 TL with an Istanbulkart (rechargeable transit card). Buy one on Day 1 if you haven't already — it saves money on all public transport.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı) in Eminönü — free to enter. Browse mountains of spices, dried fruits, Turkish delight, and teas. Buy affordable local snacks and gifts here. Then explore the surrounding Eminönü market streets — one of Istanbul's most authentic commercial districts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a Bosphorus ferry from Eminönü to Üsküdar on the Asian side (~30 TL with Istanbulkart). Walk along the Asian waterfront, visit the Mihrimah Sultan Mosque, and enjoy the different perspective of the European skyline. Explore the relaxed Üsküdar neighborhood with its local cafés and markets.
day_by_day.evening: Take the ferry back to Eminönü at sunset for golden-hour views of the Topkapi Palace, Hagia Sophia, and Blue Mosque from the water — one of Istanbul's most iconic views, completely free.

meals.breakfast: Simit with white cheese and tomatoes from a street cart near Eminönü — ~30-40 TL. Eat by the waterfront.
meals.lunch: Üsküdar has excellent local lokantas. Try Kanaat Lokantası — a historic canteen open since 1933 serving traditional Ottoman dishes at honest prices (~120-160 TL).
meals.dinner: Lentil soup and gözleme (stuffed flatbread) from a street stall or small restaurant near the hotel. Full meal under 100 TL.

day_by_day.notes: The Bosphorus ferry is one of Istanbul's best budget experiences. The short crossing offers spectacular views at a fraction of a tourist cruise price. Avoid the 'tourist Bosphorus cruise boats' which charge 10x more for a similar experience.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Fatih neighborhood — one of Istanbul's most historically dense and authentically local districts. Visit the Fatih Mosque (Fatih Camii) — free entry — built on the site of the Church of the Holy Apostles. Walk through the surrounding streets with their traditional Ottoman wooden houses.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Chora Church (Kariye Camii) in the Edirnekapı neighborhood — famous for its stunning Byzantine mosaics and frescoes. Check current access status as restoration work has been ongoing. Take a dolmuş (shared minibus) from Fatih — very cheap local transport. Walk along a section of the ancient Theodosian Walls.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Sultanahmet via public bus. Enjoy a quiet evening in the hotel neighborhood. Visit a local çay bahçesi (tea garden) in Sultanahmet Park for evening tea with Bosphorus views.

meals.breakfast: Menemen (scrambled eggs with tomatoes and peppers) at a local kahvaltı salonu in Fatih — ~80-100 TL.
meals.lunch: Street food in Fatih market area — try kokoreç (offal sandwich) if adventurous, or a simple pide from a local fırın (~60-80 TL).
meals.dinner: Asitane Restaurant near Chora Church is famous for Ottoman recipes but pricier (~300+ TL). For budget: a local kebab house in Fatih for ~130-160 TL.

day_by_day.notes: Fatih is a conservative neighborhood — dress modestly out of respect. The Theodosian Walls stretch 6.5km and walking sections is free and deeply atmospheric. Wear comfortable shoes for today's walking-heavy day.

day_by_day.morning: Take a ferry from Eminönü to the Princes' Islands (Adalar) — specifically Büyükada, the largest island. Ferry takes about 1.5 hours (~50-80 TL one way with Istanbulkart or ferry token). The islands are car-free — explore by bicycle rental (~100-150 TL for half day) or horse-drawn carriage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Climb to the Monastery of Saint George on Büyükada's hilltop for panoramic Marmara Sea views — free to visit. Explore the island's Victorian-era mansions, pine forests, and quiet beaches. Swim if weather permits.
day_by_day.evening: Take the late afternoon ferry back to the city. Arrive at Eminönü by early evening. Rest at the hotel — today is a long but rewarding day.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the hotel or grab a quick simit before the early ferry departure from Eminönü.
meals.lunch: Fresh fish lunch on Büyükada at one of the waterfront restaurants. Grilled fish with salad and bread ~200-250 TL — slightly pricier on the island but worth it for the setting.
meals.dinner: Simple and budget-friendly back in Sultanahmet — lahmacun (Turkish flatbread pizza) and ayran from a local lahmacuncu for ~80-100 TL.

day_by_day.notes: Check the IDO or Şehir Hatları ferry schedule in advance. Ferries to Büyükada depart from Eminönü and Kabataş. The first ferry can be early — plan accordingly. Fridays can be busy; book bicycle rentals early on arrival at the island.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Süleymaniye Mosque — one of Istanbul's grandest mosques, designed by the legendary architect Sinan in the 16th century. Free entry. Explore the surrounding külliye (mosque complex) with its historic tombs, medrese (school), and gardens. Stunning views of the Golden Horn.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down through the historic Tahtakale market district to the Golden Horn waterfront. Cross the Galata Bridge on foot and explore the Karaköy district. Visit the Galata Mevlevi Lodge (Galata Mevlevihanesi) — a historic tekke (dervish lodge) with a small museum (~80 TL).
day_by_day.evening: If budget allows, attend a Sema (Whirling Dervish) ceremony — authentic performances happen at Hodjapasha Cultural Center or similar venues (~250-400 TL). Alternatively, watch the free Friday/Saturday night Sema at the Galata Mevlevi Lodge if scheduled.

meals.breakfast: Turkish breakfast at a lokanta near Süleymaniye — full spread for ~100-120 TL.
meals.lunch: Tarihi Süleymaniye Kurufasülyecisi — a legendary restaurant near the mosque serving kuru fasulye (white bean stew) with rice and pickle since 1924. A complete meal for ~80-100 TL.
meals.dinner: Karaköy has excellent budget options — try a balik (fish) sandwich from a local spot or a neighborhood pide house for ~100-130 TL.

day_by_day.notes: The Süleymaniye area is less touristy than Sultanahmet, offering a more authentic Istanbul experience. The kuru fasulye restaurant near the mosque is a beloved Istanbul institution — don't miss it. Saturday means the Grand Bazaar is open if you want to revisit.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Istanbul Archaeological Museums if you haven't fully explored them yet, or head to the Turkish and Islamic Arts Museum (Türk ve İslam Eserleri Müzesi) on the Hippodrome — check if covered by Museum Pass. Excellent collection of carpets, ceramics, and calligraphy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a walk through the Balat and Fener neighborhoods along the Golden Horn — colorful, crumbling Ottoman and Greek houses, street art, and a hipster-meets-historic atmosphere. Visit the Bulgarian St. Stephen Church (Iron Church) — a neo-Gothic church made entirely of cast iron, free to enter.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Fener neighborhood's Greek Orthodox Patriarchate (Ekümenik Patrikane) — the spiritual center of Eastern Orthodox Christianity worldwide, free to visit. Return via the waterfront road with Golden Horn views.

meals.breakfast: Balat is famous for its breakfast culture. Küçük Ev or a similar Balat café for a photogenic spread — ~150-180 TL.
meals.lunch: Forno Balat or a local bakery in the neighborhood for fresh bread, börek, and pastries — ~60-80 TL.
meals.dinner: Meyhane in Balat or Fener — a local tavern with meze and grilled fish. Budget ~200-250 TL for a relaxed Sunday dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Balat and Fener are best explored on foot and are increasingly popular but still authentic. Sunday is ideal as the streets are quieter. Wear comfortable shoes — the streets are cobblestoned and hilly. The Iron Church is a genuine architectural marvel.

day_by_day.morning: Take the tram to Beyoğlu and explore the Pera neighborhood in depth. Visit the Pera Museum (Pera Müzesi) — excellent collection of Orientalist paintings and Anatolian weights (~150 TL). The famous 'Tortoise Trainer' painting by Osman Hamdi Bey is here.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through the backstreets of Cihangir — Istanbul's artsy, bohemian neighborhood with independent bookshops, antique stores, and cat-filled streets. Then head to Taksim Square and explore the surrounding streets. Visit the Republic Monument and the historic French Street (Fransız Sokağı).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Asmalımescit and Beyoğlu meyhane district for evening atmosphere. This is Istanbul's most vibrant nightlife and dining area — great for people-watching even on a budget.

meals.breakfast: Karaköy Güllüoğlu — Istanbul's most famous baklava shop, also serves breakfast pastries. Try a slice of baklava with tea for ~60-80 TL.
meals.lunch: Cihangir has many budget-friendly cafés. Try a çorba and sandwich combo at a local spot for ~100-120 TL.
meals.dinner: Beyoğlu meyhane with meze — order a selection of cold meze (hummus, haydari, patlıcan salatası) and skip the main if budget is tight. ~150-200 TL.

day_by_day.notes: Monday: most state museums are closed in Turkey, so this is a perfect day for neighborhoods, private museums, and walking. Cihangir is also famous for its cats — Istanbul is a city that loves its street cats.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Dolmabahçe Palace in Beşiktaş — the opulent 19th-century Ottoman palace on the Bosphorus waterfront. Guided tours required (admission ~300-400 TL). The palace has 285 rooms, 44 halls, and the world's largest Bohemian crystal chandelier.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the Beşiktaş waterfront to the Ortaköy neighborhood — one of Istanbul's most picturesque spots with the Ortaköy Mosque dramatically positioned beneath the Bosphorus Bridge. Explore the weekend craft market and the charming backstreets.
day_by_day.evening: Continue along the Bosphorus to Bebek neighborhood if energy allows, or take a bus back to Sultanahmet. Bebek has a beautiful waterfront promenade and is worth an evening stroll.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local pastane near Sultanahmet before heading out.
meals.lunch: Ortaköy is famous for kumpir — massive baked potatoes stuffed with toppings. A loaded kumpir from the famous stalls costs ~100-150 TL. A quintessential Istanbul street food experience.
meals.dinner: Back in Sultanahmet — try Çiğdem Pastanesi for börek and pastries, or a local pide salonu for a budget dinner under 120 TL.

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe is best visited on a weekday to avoid weekend crowds. Photography inside the palace may be restricted. The walk from Dolmabahçe to Ortaköy along the Bosphorus takes about 30-40 minutes and is very scenic — do it if weather is good.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Covered Bazaar area one final time for any last-minute shopping. Then explore the Nuruosmaniye Mosque and the Çemberlitaş (Column of Constantine) nearby — free. Walk through the Çemberlitaş Hamamı district. Consider a traditional Turkish bath (hamam) experience at Çemberlitaş Hamamı (~500-700 TL) or the more budget-friendly Gedikpaşa Hamamı (~300-400 TL).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Rüstem Pasha Mosque in Tahtakale — a hidden gem covered in the finest Iznik tiles in Istanbul, free entry, and far less visited than the Blue Mosque. Then explore the Eminönü fish market and the surrounding street food scene.
day_by_day.evening: Final Golden Horn sunset walk on the Galata Bridge. Watch the fishermen and enjoy the panorama one last time. Treat yourself to a proper farewell dinner.

meals.breakfast: A classic Turkish breakfast at Tarihi Sultanahmet Köftecisi or a nearby kahvaltı salonu.
meals.lunch: Street food tour in Eminönü — midye dolma (stuffed mussels, ~5-10 TL each), simit, and fresh fruit juice. Total ~80-100 TL.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a slightly nicer lokanta or traditional Ottoman restaurant. Try Pandeli Restaurant in the Spice Bazaar if budget allows (~300-400 TL) or a meyhane in Kumkapı neighborhood for fresh fish (~250-300 TL).

day_by_day.notes: Kumkapı is a historic fishing neighborhood near Sultanahmet with a cluster of seafood meyhanes — great for a final evening. The hamam experience, while pricier, is a bucket-list Istanbul cultural experience worth considering as a special treat.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Istanbul. Depending on departure time, take a last walk through Sultanahmet Square at dawn — the city is magical in the early morning light before the crowds arrive. Visit the Hippodrome one final time. Pick up any last souvenirs from the Arasta Bazaar.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel. Head to the airport via Marmaray or metro — budget-friendly and reliable. Allow at least 2.5-3 hours before flight for check-in and security.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Reflect on 13 incredible days in one of the world's greatest cities.

meals.breakfast: Final Turkish breakfast — make it count. A proper kahvaltı spread at a local spot near the hotel for ~120-150 TL.
meals.lunch: Airport food or a quick bite before departure. Alternatively, pack some simit, cheese, and olives from a local market for the journey.
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination.

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary tip: An Istanbulkart transit card saves significantly on all public transport. Museum Pass Istanbul covers major museums and pays for itself in 2-3 visits. Eating at lokantas, street stalls, and local bakeries rather than tourist restaurants can cut food costs by 50-70%. Istanbul is a city that rewards slow, curious exploration — the best experiences are often free.

trip_options.title: Classic Istanbul Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Travel from Istanbul Airport to Sultanahmet via Havaist bus or metro (~60–90 min). Check in to Fatih Boutique Stay and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely orientation walk around Sultanahmet Square. Admire the exterior of the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Mosque) and the Hippodrome of Constantinople (At Meydanı). Explore the Obelisk of Theodosius and the Serpent Column up close.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the nearby streets of Sultanahmet and discover the neighborhood. Visit the illuminated Blue Mosque exterior at dusk for a magical first impression of Istanbul.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or light meal at the airport before landing.
meals.lunch: Simit (sesame bread ring) and tea from a street vendor near Sultanahmet Square — quick, cheap, and authentically local (~₺50–80).
meals.dinner: Tarihi Sultanahmet Köftecisi — an iconic local institution serving classic Turkish köfte (meatballs) with bread and salad. Budget-friendly and historically significant (~₺200–300 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light due to travel fatigue. Exchange some currency at the airport or use an ATM in Sultanahmet. Buy an Istanbulkart (transit card) for easy access to trams, ferries, and buses throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Hagia Sophia Grand Mosque (Ayasofya) first thing in the morning to beat the crowds. Spend 1.5–2 hours marveling at the Byzantine mosaics, massive dome, and layered history of this 1,500-year-old monument. Dress modestly and bring a headscarf if needed.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk five minutes to the Topkapı Palace — the heart of the Ottoman Empire for 400 years. Explore the Imperial Treasury (featuring the Topkapi Dagger and Spoonmaker's Diamond), the Harem quarters (separate ticket), and panoramic views of the Bosphorus.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the backstreets of Sultanahmet toward the Arasta Bazaar, a quieter alternative to the Grand Bazaar for browsing ceramics, textiles, and Turkish crafts without aggressive sales pressure.

meals.breakfast: Full traditional Turkish breakfast (kahvaltı) at the hotel or a nearby café — olives, white cheese, tomatoes, cucumbers, eggs, honey, clotted cream, and tea.
meals.lunch: Havuzlu Restaurant inside or near the Grand Bazaar area — traditional Ottoman-Turkish dishes in a historic setting (~₺300–450 per person).
meals.dinner: Balıkçı Sabahattin — a beloved old-school fish restaurant near Sultanahmet, family-run since 1927. Try fresh grilled fish with mezes (~₺500–700 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Topkapı Palace is closed on Tuesdays — Sunday is a great day to visit. Buy a Museum Pass Istanbul (covers Topkapı, Hagia Sophia archaeological areas, and more) if you plan to visit multiple museums — it pays off quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı) — the stunning 6th-century underground Byzantine water reservoir with atmospheric lighting, Medusa head columns, and mysterious walkways. Spend about 1 hour here.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Istanbul Archaeological Museums complex (Arkeoloji Müzeleri) — three museums in one, featuring the Alexander Sarcophagus, ancient Anatolian artifacts, and the Museum of the Ancient Orient. One of the most underrated sites in the city.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Beyoğlu district via tram and funicular. Walk up İstiklal Avenue (İstiklal Caddesi), Istanbul's famous pedestrian boulevard lined with 19th-century European architecture, bookshops, cafés, and street musicians.

meals.breakfast: Van Kahvaltı Evi near Sultanahmet — famous for its lavish southeastern Turkish breakfast spread with over 20 items including herb cheeses and honey (~₺250–350 per person).
meals.lunch: Lezzet-i Şahane or a similar lokanta (traditional Turkish canteen) near the Archaeological Museums — home-cooked dishes like lentil soup, stuffed peppers, and lamb stew (~₺150–250).
meals.dinner: Çiçek Pasajı (Flower Passage) area off İstiklal Avenue — dine at one of the meyhanes (taverns) for rakı, mezes, and live fasıl music in a vibrant atmosphere (~₺400–600 per person).

day_by_day.notes: The Basilica Cistern recently underwent renovation — check current opening hours before visiting. The Archaeological Museums are often overlooked by tourists but are world-class — allow at least 2–3 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı) — one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets with over 4,000 shops. Explore the hans (caravanserais), jewelry sections, spice dealers, and carpet galleries. Bargaining is expected and part of the experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk downhill to the Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı) in Eminönü. Browse aromatic stalls of Turkish spices, dried fruits, lokum (Turkish delight), and teas. Explore the surrounding streets of Eminönü for a glimpse of everyday Istanbul life.
day_by_day.evening: Take a short ferry ride from Eminönü across the Golden Horn to Karaköy. Explore the trendy Karaköy neighborhood with its galleries, design shops, and waterfront cafés.

meals.breakfast: Simit Sarayı or a local bakery near the hotel — simit, börek (flaky pastry), and tea for an authentic quick breakfast (~₺80–120).
meals.lunch: Pandeli Restaurant above the Spice Bazaar entrance — a historic restaurant serving classic Ottoman-Turkish cuisine in beautiful tiled rooms since 1901. Reservation recommended (~₺400–600 per person).
meals.dinner: Karaköy Lokantası — a stylish yet approachable meyhane-style restaurant in Karaköy with excellent mezes and seafood (~₺450–650 per person).

day_by_day.notes: The Grand Bazaar is closed on Sundays. Tuesday is a great day to visit. Carry cash (Turkish Lira) for the bazaars — many small vendors don't accept cards. Watch your belongings in crowded areas.

day_by_day.morning: Take a full Bosphorus cruise — board a public ferry from Eminönü (Şehir Hatları) for the classic long Bosphorus tour (~2.5 hours each way, very affordable). Sail past Ottoman palaces, wooden yalıs (waterfront mansions), and the two continents bridged by iconic suspension bridges.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disembark at Anadolu Kavağı (the Asian-side terminus) and hike up to the ruins of Yoros Castle for sweeping views where the Bosphorus meets the Black Sea. Explore the small fishing village below.
day_by_day.evening: Return by ferry to Eminönü and walk across the Galata Bridge, watching local fishermen cast their lines as the sun sets over the minarets of the old city.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or grab a fresh simit and tea from a cart near Eminönü before boarding the ferry.
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish (balık ekmek) or seafood at one of the casual restaurants in Anadolu Kavağı village — known for excellent Black Sea–style fish (~₺300–450 per person).
meals.dinner: Under the Galata Bridge at one of the fish restaurants on the lower level — fresh catch of the day with rakı and mezes, with views of the illuminated old city (~₺400–550 per person).

day_by_day.notes: The public Şehir Hatları Bosphorus ferry is far more affordable than private tour boats and offers the same views. Buy tickets with your Istanbulkart. Bring a light jacket — it can be breezy on the water even in May.

day_by_day.morning: Cross to the Asian side of Istanbul via ferry from Eminönü to Kadıköy (~25 min). Explore the vibrant Kadıköy Market (Kadıköy Çarşısı) — a foodie paradise with fresh produce, fish, cheese, olives, and street food stalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wander through the Moda neighborhood of Kadıköy — a charming, bohemian district with tree-lined streets, independent cafés, vintage shops, and a relaxed local atmosphere far from tourist crowds. Walk along the Moda waterfront promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the European side via ferry. Visit the Galata Tower (Galata Kulesi) at sunset for panoramic 360-degree views of Istanbul, the Bosphorus, and the Golden Horn.

meals.breakfast: Çiya Sofrası in Kadıköy — a legendary restaurant serving rare regional Anatolian dishes for breakfast and all day. Try dishes you won't find elsewhere (~₺200–350 per person).
meals.lunch: Street food tour of Kadıköy Market: kokoreç (offal sandwich), midye dolma (stuffed mussels), and fresh ayran (yogurt drink) from market stalls (~₺150–200 total).
meals.dinner: Zübeyir Ocakbaşı near Galata — a beloved charcoal grill restaurant known for exceptional kebabs, mezes, and grilled vegetables in a warm, smoky atmosphere (~₺400–600 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Kadıköy is a must for food lovers — it represents the authentic, non-touristy Istanbul. The Galata Tower has an entry fee; arrive 30–40 minutes before sunset for the best light and manageable queues.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Süleymaniye Mosque — Sinan's masterpiece and arguably the most beautiful mosque in Istanbul, built for Suleiman the Magnificent in 1557. Explore the surrounding külliye (mosque complex) including the tombs of Suleiman and Roxelana.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the historic neighborhood of Zeyrek and the Church of Christ Pantocrator (Zeyrek Camii) — a stunning 12th-century Byzantine monastery church that rivals Hagia Sophia in historical significance but sees far fewer visitors. Wander the wooden Ottoman houses of the Zeyrek hillside.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Balat — Istanbul's most atmospheric and photogenic historic neighborhood, formerly the Jewish and Greek quarter, now a hub of colorful houses, street art, and trendy cafés.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a neighborhood bakkal (corner store) near the hotel.
meals.lunch: Darüzziyafe Restaurant inside the Süleymaniye complex — a historic Ottoman soup kitchen turned restaurant serving traditional Ottoman cuisine in a beautiful courtyard (~₺350–500 per person).
meals.dinner: Fener & Balat neighborhood restaurant — try Köfteci Ramiz or a local meyhane in Balat for simple, honest Turkish food in a colorful setting (~₺250–400 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Friday is the Islamic holy day — the Süleymaniye Mosque will be very active around midday prayers. Be respectful of prayer times. Balat and Fener are best explored on foot — wear comfortable shoes as the streets are cobblestoned and hilly.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Dolmabahçe Palace (Dolmabahçe Sarayı) in Beşiktaş — the opulent 19th-century Ottoman palace on the Bosphorus shore, blending European Baroque with Ottoman aesthetics. Tour the Selamlık (ceremonial rooms) including the world's largest Bohemian crystal chandelier.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short bus ride to the Beşiktaş neighborhood. Explore the lively Beşiktaş fish market and waterfront. Visit the Çırağan Palace (now a luxury hotel) for a glimpse of its stunning exterior on the Bosphorus.
day_by_day.evening: Continue up to the Ortaköy neighborhood — one of Istanbul's most picturesque spots, with its baroque waterfront mosque framed by the Bosphorus Bridge. Browse artisan stalls and enjoy the lively waterfront atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Turkish breakfast at a café in Beşiktaş near the ferry terminal — full spread with eggs, pastries, and tea (~₺200–300 per person).
meals.lunch: Beşiktaş fish market area — fresh fish sandwiches (balık ekmek) or a casual seafood lokanta (~₺200–300 per person).
meals.dinner: Ortaköy kumpir (giant stuffed baked potato) from the famous street stalls — a beloved Istanbul street food tradition. Pair with waffles for dessert (~₺150–200 total for a casual street food dinner).

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe Palace requires guided tours (included in ticket price) and has timed entry slots — book tickets online in advance or arrive early. The palace is closed on Mondays and Thursdays.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Istanbul Modern (İstanbul Modern) — Turkey's premier contemporary art museum, recently reopened in a stunning new building in Karaköy designed by Renzo Piano. Explore rotating exhibitions of Turkish and international modern art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through the Tophane neighborhood and up to the Galata district. Visit the Galata Mevlevi Lodge (Galata Mevlevihanesi) — a beautifully restored 15th-century Sufi lodge and museum dedicated to the Mevlevi Order (the whirling dervishes).
day_by_day.evening: Attend a Sema ceremony — a traditional whirling dervish performance at the Hodjapasha Cultural Center in Sirkeci or another licensed venue. A deeply spiritual and mesmerizing experience (~₺400–600 per person).

meals.breakfast: Karaköy Güllüoğlu — the most famous baklava shop in Istanbul, serving fresh baklava and börek for breakfast with tea. An indulgent Istanbul institution (~₺150–250).
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at a modern café in Galata — try menemen (Turkish scrambled eggs with tomatoes and peppers) or a pide (Turkish flatbread pizza) (~₺200–300 per person).
meals.dinner: Dinner before the Sema ceremony — Sirkeci area has many traditional restaurants. Try Hafız Mustafa's restaurant or a nearby lokanta for hearty Turkish classics (~₺300–450 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book the Sema ceremony tickets in advance — performances often sell out, especially on weekends. The ceremony lasts approximately 1 hour and is a non-religious cultural performance open to all visitors.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Chora Church (Kariye Camii / Chora Museum) — a 14th-century Byzantine church containing what many art historians consider the finest Byzantine mosaics and frescoes in existence, even more detailed than Hagia Sophia's. Located in the Edirnekapı neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the ancient Theodosian Walls (Kara Surları) — the massive 5th-century land walls that protected Constantinople for over 1,000 years. Explore the partially restored sections near Edirnekapı and the Yedikule Fortress.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Sultanahmet and visit the Turkish and Islamic Arts Museum (Türk ve İslam Eserleri Müzesi) on the Hippodrome — home to one of the world's greatest collections of Islamic art, carpets, and calligraphy.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a neighborhood bakery near Sultanahmet.
meals.lunch: Local esnaf lokantası (workers' restaurant) near Edirnekapı — daily rotating home-cooked dishes like kuru fasulye (white bean stew), pilaf, and soup. Authentic and very affordable (~₺100–180 per person).
meals.dinner: Asitane Restaurant near the Chora Church — specializes in historically researched Ottoman palace recipes from the 15th–17th centuries. A unique and memorable dining experience (~₺500–700 per person).

day_by_day.notes: The Chora Church status (mosque/museum) may change — verify current access before visiting. The Theodosian Walls are largely unrestored in sections — wear sturdy shoes and be cautious when exploring. The walk along the walls is free.

day_by_day.morning: Take a ferry from Kabataş to the Princes' Islands (Adalar) — specifically Büyükada, the largest island (~1.5 hour ferry). Arrive and rent a bicycle or hire a horse-drawn phaeton carriage (the islands have no motorized vehicles). Explore the Victorian-era Greek mansions, pine forests, and hilltop monastery of Aya Yorgi.
day_by_day.afternoon: Swim at one of Büyükada's small beaches (Yörük Ali or Nakibend), or continue exploring the island's quiet lanes, old Greek Orthodox churches, and panoramic viewpoints. Enjoy the peaceful pace of island life.
day_by_day.evening: Return ferry to Istanbul (last ferries depart early evening). Arrive back in Sultanahmet and enjoy a relaxed evening stroll around the illuminated monuments.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before departure — grab a simit and tea at the Kabataş ferry terminal.
meals.lunch: Lunch at one of Büyükada's waterfront fish restaurants — fresh Marmara Sea fish, mezes, and cold drinks on a terrace overlooking the sea (~₺350–500 per person).
meals.dinner: Back in Sultanahmet — Mozaik Restaurant, a reliable mid-range option near the hotel serving classic Turkish dishes in a warm, tiled interior (~₺300–450 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Check the Şehir Hatları ferry schedule carefully — service frequency varies by season. In May, ferries run regularly. The island gets crowded on summer weekends — a Tuesday visit is ideal. Bring sunscreen and water.

day_by_day.morning: Revisit any favorite sites or explore the Küçük Ayasofya (Little Hagia Sophia) — a stunning 6th-century Byzantine church converted to a mosque, often overlooked but architecturally remarkable. Located just south of Sultanahmet in a quiet neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Pera Museum (Pera Müzesi) in Beyoğlu — a superb private museum housing the famous 'Tortoise Trainer' painting by Osman Hamdi Bey, Anatolian weights and measures, and rotating international exhibitions. Then explore the Pera/Beyoğlu backstreets.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell evening — take a sunset ferry from Eminönü to Üsküdar on the Asian side for golden-hour views of the old city skyline, the Maiden's Tower (Kız Kulesi), and the Bosphorus. Return via ferry for a final walk through Sultanahmet.

meals.breakfast: Splurge on a final elaborate Turkish breakfast at Namı Diğer or a similar breakfast café in Beyoğlu (~₺300–400 per person).
meals.lunch: Haci Abdullah Restaurant in Beyoğlu — Istanbul's oldest continuously operating restaurant (founded 1888), serving classic Ottoman-Turkish cuisine in a historic setting (~₺350–550 per person).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Matbah Restaurant inside the Ottoman Hotel Imperial near Hagia Sophia — elegant Ottoman palace cuisine with stunning views of the Blue Mosque. A special splurge for the last evening (~₺600–900 per person).

day_by_day.notes: The Maiden's Tower (Kız Kulesi) has been restored and reopened as a café/restaurant — you can take a short boat from Üsküdar to visit it if interested (book ahead). This is a good day to finalize souvenir shopping and pack.

day_by_day.morning: Depending on departure flight time — final morning walk through Sultanahmet. Visit the Hippodrome one last time, photograph the Blue Mosque in the morning light, and pick up any last-minute gifts from the Arasta Bazaar.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel. Head to Istanbul Airport via Havaist bus or metro from Sultanahmet (allow 90–120 minutes for travel + airport procedures). Depart Istanbul.
day_by_day.evening: In transit or at destination.

meals.breakfast: Final Turkish breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café — savor the last çay (tea) and fresh bread.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the hotel before checkout, or at the airport — try the airport's Turkish food options rather than international chains.
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight.

day_by_day.notes: Allow ample time for the airport journey — Istanbul traffic can be unpredictable. Havaist buses run directly from Sultanahmet/Taksim to Istanbul Airport. Keep some Turkish Lira for last-minute purchases and tips. Confirm flight details the night before.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Istanbul Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Istanbul Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from Istanbul Airport to Sultanahmet Square boutique hotel. Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your premium suite overlooking the historic district.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk around Sultanahmet Square. Admire the exterior of the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Mosque) and the Hagia Sophia from the plaza. Stroll through the Hippodrome of Constantinople, viewing the Obelisk of Theodosius and the Serpent Column at a leisurely pace.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome dinner at Matbah Ottoman Palace Cuisine, a celebrated restaurant inside the Ottoman Imperial Hotel steps from the palace walls, offering an authentic Ottoman tasting menu with dishes sourced from 15th-century imperial recipes.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Light mezze and Turkish tea at Tarihi Sultanahmet Köftecisi or a café near the hotel upon arrival
meals.dinner: Matbah Ottoman Palace Cuisine — multi-course Ottoman tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Flight LH arrives 13:00. Pre-arrange private airport transfer with your hotel concierge. Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Hagia Sophia (Ayasofya). Explore the Byzantine mosaics, imperial galleries, and the stunning dome with an expert historian guide. Arrive early to beat crowds. Afterward, visit the nearby Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı) for its atmospheric underground columns and illuminated waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Topkapi Palace with a private guide. Visit the Imperial Treasury (home to the Topkapi Dagger and Spoonmaker's Diamond), the Harem quarters, and the sacred relics pavilion. Enjoy the panoramic Bosphorus views from the palace terraces.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the terrace of the Four Seasons Istanbul at Sultanahmet, followed by dinner at Seasons Restaurant, renowned for its refined Turkish-Mediterranean cuisine and impeccable service.

meals.breakfast: Lavish Turkish breakfast spread at the hotel — cheeses, olives, sucuk, menemen, fresh breads, and honey
meals.lunch: Private picnic lunch arranged by the hotel concierge in Topkapi Palace gardens, or lunch at Konyalı Topkapı Restaurant inside the palace grounds
meals.dinner: Seasons Restaurant at the Four Seasons Sultanahmet — contemporary Turkish fine dining

day_by_day.notes: Book Hagia Sophia and Topkapi Palace skip-the-line tickets well in advance. Harem requires a separate ticket. Modest dress required for Hagia Sophia (head covering for women).

day_by_day.morning: Private tour of the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Mosque) — explore the intricate Iznik tile work, six minarets, and the vast prayer hall with an expert guide. Then visit the nearby Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts (Ibrahim Pasha Palace) for world-class carpets, calligraphy, and Ottoman artifacts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Immersive Grand Bazaar experience with a private shopping guide. Navigate the 4,000-shop labyrinth focusing on antique jewelry, hand-painted ceramics, silk textiles, and rare spices. Your guide will introduce you to trusted artisans and negotiate authentically on your behalf.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Neolokal, one of Istanbul's most acclaimed fine-dining restaurants by chef Maksut Aşkar, located in the SALT Galata building. The menu celebrates Anatolian ingredients with modern technique.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Traditional Turkish lunch at Havuzlu Restaurant inside the Grand Bazaar — a hidden gem serving home-style Turkish dishes
meals.dinner: Neolokal — Anatolian-inspired tasting menu with natural wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Grand Bazaar is closed on Sundays; Monday is ideal. Carry cash (Turkish Lira) for bazaar purchases. Neolokal reservation is essential — book weeks in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı) and the surrounding Eminönü waterfront. Sample exotic spices, Turkish delight, dried fruits, and lokum with a food expert. Then cross the Galata Bridge on foot, watching fishermen and absorbing the Golden Horn views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ascend the Galata Tower for panoramic city views, then explore the bohemian Galata and Karaköy neighborhoods. Visit a master calligrapher's atelier and browse contemporary art galleries. Explore the historic Tunnel (Tünel), one of the world's oldest underground railways.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Mikla, perched atop the Marmara Pera hotel with sweeping 360° views of Istanbul. Chef Mehmet Gürs serves New Anatolian cuisine — a refined fusion of Turkish and Nordic culinary traditions.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Fresh fish sandwich (balık ekmek) from a traditional boat vendor at Eminönü, followed by Turkish tea at a waterfront çay bahçesi
meals.dinner: Mikla Restaurant — New Anatolian tasting menu with panoramic Bosphorus views

day_by_day.notes: Mikla is one of Istanbul's top restaurants — reservations essential. The Galata Tower can be crowded; visit mid-afternoon for the best experience.

day_by_day.morning: Private full-day Bosphorus cruise begins. Board a private yacht from Kabataş or Beşiktaş pier. Cruise the European and Asian shores, passing Dolmabahçe Palace, Çırağan Palace, the Bosphorus Bridge, and the Rumeli Fortress (Rumelihisarı). Stop to explore the fortress up close.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the private Bosphorus cruise northward toward the Black Sea entrance. Stop at the charming fishing village of Anadolu Kavağı on the Asian side for lunch. Hike up to the Yoros Castle ruins for spectacular views of where the Bosphorus meets the Black Sea.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Sultanahmet by private transfer. Relaxing hammam experience at the historic Ayasofya Hürrem Sultan Hamamı (built by Sinan in 1556), the most luxurious traditional Turkish bath in the city, with a private VIP suite treatment.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a waterfront restaurant in Anadolu Kavağı — grilled sea bass, calamari, and mezes
meals.dinner: Light dinner at Balıkçı Sabahattin, an iconic fish restaurant in Sultanahmet serving the freshest Bosphorus catch since 1927

day_by_day.notes: Book the private yacht well in advance through the hotel concierge. Hürrem Sultan Hamamı VIP suite must be reserved ahead. Bring a change of clothes for the hammam.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Dolmabahçe Palace on the European Bosphorus shore. Marvel at the 285-room palace, the world's largest Bohemian crystal chandelier (a gift from Queen Victoria), and the ornate ceremonial halls. This was Atatürk's residence in his final years.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the upscale Nişantaşı neighborhood — Istanbul's answer to Milan's fashion district. Browse flagship stores of Turkish designers (Vakko, Beymen), visit the Pera Museum featuring Orientalist paintings and the famous 'Tortoise Trainer' by Osman Hamdi Bey.
day_by_day.evening: Private rooftop dinner experience at Çırağan Palace Kempinski's Tuğra Restaurant, set inside a 19th-century Ottoman palace on the Bosphorus. Exceptional Ottoman-Turkish cuisine in a setting of unmatched grandeur.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch at Sunset Grill & Bar in Ulus, with spectacular panoramic Bosphorus and city views
meals.dinner: Tuğra Restaurant, Çırağan Palace Kempinski — Ottoman imperial cuisine with Bosphorus views

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe Palace is closed on Mondays and Thursdays — verify current schedule. Tuğra Restaurant reservation essential. Smart-casual dress code at both dinner venues.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Princes' Islands (Adalar). Take a private speedboat from Kabataş to Büyükada, the largest island. Explore by horse-drawn carriage (phaeton) or bicycle through pine forests and Victorian-era mansions. Visit the Greek Orthodox Monastery of St. George on the hilltop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely afternoon on Büyükada — swim at a private beach club, explore the charming town center, and browse local artisan shops. Enjoy the peaceful, car-free atmosphere that feels worlds away from the city.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Istanbul by private speedboat at sunset. Dinner at 360 Istanbul on İstiklal Avenue — a stylish rooftop restaurant with breathtaking 360° views of the Golden Horn, Bosphorus, and city skyline.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at Milto Restaurant on Büyükada, a beloved island institution serving grilled fish and mezes
meals.dinner: 360 Istanbul — contemporary Turkish and Mediterranean cuisine with panoramic city views

day_by_day.notes: Private speedboat to Princes' Islands is significantly faster than the public ferry. Book in advance. The island is very popular in May — arrive early for the best experience.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Chora Church (Kariye Mosque/Museum) in the Edirnekapı neighborhood — home to the world's finest surviving Byzantine mosaics and frescoes from the 14th century. Then walk along the ancient Theodosian Land Walls, a UNESCO World Heritage site stretching 6.5 km.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Fener and Balat neighborhoods — Istanbul's most colorful and historically layered districts. Explore the Greek Orthodox Patriarchate, the Bulgarian Iron Church (St. Stephen of the Bulgars), and the Jewish heritage sites with a private cultural guide. Browse vintage shops and street art.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a rooftop bar in Balat overlooking the Golden Horn. Dinner at Alancha in Karaköy, a Michelin-recognized restaurant by chef İbrahim Gündoğdu, offering an avant-garde Anatolian tasting menu.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional lokanta in Balat — try kuru fasulye, stuffed vegetables, and ayran in an authentic neighborhood setting
meals.dinner: Alancha — avant-garde Anatolian tasting menu, one of Istanbul's most innovative dining experiences

day_by_day.notes: Chora Church may have restricted access depending on ongoing restoration work — verify status before visiting. Balat is best explored on foot. Comfortable walking shoes recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Private cooking class with a master Turkish chef. Learn to prepare a full Ottoman-Turkish feast: red lentil soup, börek, lamb kebab, stuffed grape leaves (dolma), and baklava. Held in a traditional Ottoman kitchen setting in Sultanahmet.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Istanbul Archaeology Museums (Arkeoloji Müzeleri) — a trio of world-class museums housing the Alexander Sarcophagus, Sidon Royal Necropolis, and an extraordinary collection of ancient artifacts from across the Ottoman Empire's former territories.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset cruise on the Bosphorus aboard a gulet (traditional wooden sailing vessel). Sip champagne as the sun sets over the minarets and the two continents glow golden. Dinner served on board by a private chef.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Enjoy the fruits of your cooking class — sit down to eat the meal you prepared with your chef and fellow participants
meals.dinner: Private chef dinner aboard a Bosphorus gulet — fresh seafood, mezes, and Turkish wines under the stars

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class and private gulet cruise through the hotel concierge well in advance. The Archaeology Museums are closed on Mondays — Sunday is ideal.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Asian side of Istanbul. Take a private water taxi across the Bosphorus to Kadıköy. Visit the vibrant Kadıköy Market (Tarihi Kadıköy Çarşısı) for artisan cheeses, cured meats, fresh produce, and specialty foods with a local food guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through the charming Moda neighborhood — explore independent bookshops, vintage boutiques, and art galleries. Visit the historic Haydarpaşa Train Station (exterior), a stunning neo-Gothic structure on the Asian shore. Walk along the Moda seafront promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Çiya Sofrası in Kadıköy, one of the most celebrated restaurants in Turkey. Chef Musa Dağdeviren is a culinary anthropologist who resurrects forgotten Anatolian recipes from across Turkey's diverse regions.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Kokoreç and midye dolma (stuffed mussels) street food tour in Kadıköy with your food guide
meals.dinner: Çiya Sofrası — legendary Anatolian regional cuisine, a James Beard Award-recognized institution

day_by_day.notes: The Asian side offers a completely different atmosphere from the European side — more local, less touristy. Private water taxi is more flexible than the public ferry.

day_by_day.morning: Private tour of the Süleymaniye Mosque, the masterpiece of Ottoman architect Mimar Sinan, built for Suleiman the Magnificent. Explore the mosque complex, the tombs of Suleiman and Roxelana, and the surrounding külliye (social complex). Then visit Sinan's tomb nearby.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the historic Beyazıt neighborhood and the Istanbul University campus. Visit the Beyazıt Mosque (Istanbul's oldest imperial mosque), then browse the renowned second-hand book market (Sahaflar Çarşısı). Afterward, explore the Zeyrek neighborhood and the Byzantine Pantokrator Monastery.
day_by_day.evening: Private wine tasting and dinner at Nicole Restaurant in Tomtom Suites, featuring the finest Turkish wines from Cappadocia, Thrace, and the Aegean, paired with a sophisticated contemporary Turkish tasting menu.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Traditional Turkish lunch at Darüzziyafe, a historic restaurant in the Süleymaniye külliye complex serving Ottoman recipes in a 16th-century soup kitchen setting
meals.dinner: Nicole Restaurant — contemporary Turkish fine dining with curated Turkish wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Darüzziyafe is one of Istanbul's most historically significant dining venues. Nicole Restaurant is highly regarded — reservations essential.

day_by_day.morning: Private visit to a master ceramicist's atelier to learn about and try traditional Iznik tile painting — a centuries-old Ottoman art form. Then visit the Sakıp Sabancı Museum in Emirgan, one of Turkey's finest private museums, housing Ottoman calligraphy, paintings, and rotating international exhibitions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through Emirgan Park — Istanbul's most beautiful public park, famous for its tulip gardens (especially stunning in May). Visit the historic Emirgan Mosque and the charming wooden kiosks. Take a private car along the upper Bosphorus road for scenic views.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell pre-dinner cocktails at the rooftop bar of the Soho House Istanbul in Beyoğlu. Final gala dinner at Feriye Lokantası, set inside a 19th-century Ottoman palace pavilion on the Bosphorus waterfront in Ortaköy, with the illuminated Bosphorus Bridge as your backdrop.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch at Emirgan Sütiş, a beloved historic café in Emirgan Park serving traditional Turkish pastries, künefe, and light meals
meals.dinner: Feriye Lokantası — Ottoman-Turkish cuisine in a spectacular Bosphorus palace setting

day_by_day.notes: The Iznik tile atelier experience should be arranged through the hotel concierge. Emirgan Park is particularly beautiful in May with blooming tulips. Feriye reservation essential.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisurely morning in Istanbul. Return to your favorite spots in Sultanahmet for last photographs — the Blue Mosque at dawn is magical. Visit the Arasta Bazaar beneath the Blue Mosque for last-minute premium souvenirs: hand-painted ceramics, silk scarves, and artisan jewelry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last Turkish breakfast or brunch at the hotel. Private luxury transfer to Istanbul Airport for your departure flight. En route, optional stop at a premium Turkish delight shop (Hafız Mustafa or Ali Muhiddin Hacı Bekir) for gourmet gifts to take home.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Istanbul. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days in one of the world's greatest cities.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell Turkish breakfast at the hotel — the full spread one last time
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch or mezze at a terrace restaurant near Sultanahmet before transfer
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for Istanbul Airport. Pre-arrange private transfer. Confirm luggage allowance for any ceramics or fragile purchases. Currency exchange at the airport before departure if needed.
